scope: Read-only assessment of an optional Linux-container environment for future Playground variants.

recommendation.current: Keep host-native Windows with child-local MXC for the next separately ordered Conventional attempt: real coding/tests worked; resolve repository Git approval and controller integration before changing the environment. Do not change environments mid-study.
recommendation.future: Add an optional, separately identified Linux-container environment stratum after adapter contract integration. First run a bounded provider-free readiness check and measure setup/cold-start cost; authorize a model trajectory only after that check.
rationale: Inference: Linux Codex CLI inside a Linux container uses the Linux sandbox path rather than native Windows sandboxing, which could avoid a Windows-specific failure. It changes OS, shell, filesystem, process and helper behavior, so it cannot establish that the Windows failure is fixed.
Docker Desktop on Windows still depends on Windows plus WSL2 or a VM backend, and adds engine, image, mount, resource and lifecycle setup.
Codex ChatGPT-account authentication has official headless/container routes. API-key or Agents API migration is not required.
recommendation.appliesTo: Historical 2026-10-09 decision for the then-ordered Windows Conventional attempt. It does not select the environment for a new comparison; see stabilizationAddendum.recommendationNow for the updated prospective recommendation.

facts: For headless/remote CLI, Codex recommends beta device-code auth when enabled in account/workspace settings.
Official fallback: authenticate where a browser is available and copy ~/.codex/auth.json into the container.
auth.json contains access tokens and must be treated like a password. OS credential-store auth may not support this file-copy fallback; file-based storage is an explicit setting.
API keys are recommended by the guide as the default for automation, but ChatGPT login is explicitly supported.
implications: Prefer device-code login if enabled, otherwise deliberately use file-based auth cache; do not mount the full host home or .codex directory.
Exclude credentials from Git, logs, snapshots and evidence manifests. Record method/readiness only.
Specify how refreshed auth state is persisted or discarded without exposing token values.

facts: Codex uses native Windows sandbox from PowerShell and Linux sandbox implementation from WSL2.
Linux/WSL2 sandbox uses bubblewrap when available or a bundled helper requiring unprivileged user-namespace support.
codexSandbox.inference: A Linux Codex CLI in a Linux container may avoid the native Windows sandbox path, but nested namespace restrictions may prevent Linux sandbox startup. Verify with the chosen backend; do not disable sandboxing or broaden host policy.

facts: Docker Desktop uses WSL2 by default for Linux containers; other VM backends depend on install/edition.
Docker Desktop needs Windows virtualization/WSL prerequisites and remains hosted by Windows.
Docker recommends storing bind-mounted Linux source in the Linux filesystem for performance and file-change events; Windows filesystem mounts can be slower.
Claude Code supports Dev Containers and browser authentication inside them.
Browser callback may not reach the container; documented fallback is manually entering the displayed code.
Container home is discarded on rebuild by default. Persisting auth requires a named volume plus CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR because account/config data also resides in a separate file.
Dev Container Feature installs latest and auto-updates by default; pinning requires explicit version install and disabling updates.

bindPerRun: model, effort, helper settings, sandbox and approval rights
image acquisition/build and environment startup time
lifecycle: Use disposable per-run container/workspace; do not mount host home, SSH material, or broad credential directories.
Keep auth outside tracked/evidence paths, restrict access, and define refresh-state retention/cleanup.
Adapter must account for container, CLI, app-server and owned helper startup and shutdown.
studyDesign.firstCheck: Provider-free readiness only: engine available, pinned image ready, expected CLI version available, sandbox starts under container restrictions, public workspace mount works, and auth readiness route is available without exposing credentials. Measure wall time; stop on concrete failure.

limitations.note: Documentation review only; runtime behavior on this Windows installation remains unverified.

correction.priorClaim: Initial read-only assessment incorrectly said no authoritative Codex ChatGPT-account container-auth route had been found, suggesting API-key/Agents API might be necessary.
correction.correctedFinding: That was wrong. The official Codex auth page explicitly documents device-code auth for headless use and copying auth.json into Docker. Auth remains a security/lifecycle concern, not a reason to exclude containers or switch providers.

causeAssessment.status: reproduced on the actual A01 README; Git considers it unchanged

causeAssessment.status: observed in prior native attempts; original Host-path native editing worked
causeAssessment.owner: Runtime workspace identity and tool launch
causeAssessment.repair: Verify actual tool CWD and keep one canonical workspace identity; preserve shell errors even when process exit is zero.

causeAssessment.cause: Windows sharing violation while appending a live journal
causeAssessment.status: actual append failed; restrictive reader mechanism reproduced on owned scratch; exact live lock holder unknown
causeAssessment.owner: Product owns journal/append correctness and recovery; Playground/operator owns the non-blocking live-audit reader.
causeAssessment.repair: Audit with short explicit FileShare.ReadWrite|FileShare.Delete reads, close the handle before parsing; preserve bounded original failure and recovery receipts.
causeAssessment.linuxEffect: Avoids Windows sharing-mode semantics; journal correctness and recovery still require repair.

causeAssessment.status: source-backed findings; Product repairs in progress; helper cleanup was not the observed Actual15 cause

localInventory.method: Read-only wsl --list --verbose, docker context ls and short non-login Ubuntu commands; no installs, restart, container creation, credential read or model calls.

userNamespaceCheck.kernelUnprivilegedUsernsCloneFile: absent; this does not prove namespaces unsupported

localInventory.limitations: PATH inventory does not establish absence from the whole installation; Windows npm starter was not invoked; no login status, model access, sandbox execution or product runtime was tested.

recommendationNow.immediate: Finish the demonstrated byte-domain and recovery repairs on the preserved Product attempt. Make live audits non-blocking. Use provider-free targeted regressions before another separately authorized native run.
recommendationNow.nextSharedEnvironment: Prepare WSL2 with native Linux Codex and product/tool binaries; keep repositories, workspaces, temp files, app-server and journals in the Linux filesystem under an owned /home path. Use the same prospective environment for Conventional and Markitect.
recommendationNow.container: Defer Docker as the immediate rescue. It adds image, engine, mounts, nested sandbox, resource and authentication lifecycle. Revisit a pinned image when repeatable disposable environments or stronger isolation justify that work.
recommendationNow.windowsCoverage: Preserve historical Windows failures and working MXC evidence. Verify supported Windows behavior with targeted regressions; do not require an extra full scientific comparison merely because a platform option exists.
recommendationNow.studyBoundary: Do not pool prior Windows and new Linux runs or retrospectively change their outcomes. CLI/MCP/App Server transport choice does not choose the OS; record transport and execution environment separately.
recommendationNow.ownership: Environment provisioning/preflight belongs to the Playground execution boundary; product install/config/MCP/App Server lifecycle remains variant-owned. All related processes and filesystem identities must stay in the selected environment.
recommendationNow.decisionStatus: Scientist recommendation for coordination; WSL migration has not been executed or selected by a frozen study order.

finiteReadinessBeforeModelWork: Verify all executable paths resolve to pinned Linux binaries, not /mnt/c wrappers; record actual versions and digests.
Prepare a disposable public repository under the owned Linux filesystem; confirm CWD, Git filter equivalence and exact preview-to-write bytes.
Check the selected CLI sandbox can read/write only the declared scratch/workspace and that concurrent auditing does not block append; no provider required.

As a bounded setup/preflight action, initialize the native App Server and check admission using the selected local configuration; the variant owns created processes/state and shutdown. Protocol readiness remains separate from model/tool access.
Use a separately established login without reading or publishing credentials; a missing login remains an explicit blocker.
Run targeted Markitect byte/recovery/helper lifecycle regressions; Linux alone is not acceptance.
Only then bind a fresh finite execution to both method and environment inputs; this assessment starts no model trajectory.
stabilizationAddendum.authConclusion: Codex ChatGPT login has official device-code/headless/container routes, so API-key migration is not required. Claude documents container browser-code login and auth persistence. Neither Linux login was tested here.
